newsitem.title: UK: Europe nickel premiums up on producer problems.
newsitem.headline: Europe nickel premiums up on producer problems.

text.p: Premiums for physical nickel have edged up and business has been brisk due in part to recent production disruptions, physical traders said on Tuesday.
"We've having more inquiries than usual this time of year," one trader said.
"I don't think it's because demand is improving, as consumers are still buying hand to mouth, but it appears the producers have pulled back a little."
Traders noted the explosion at Outokumpu's Harjavalta smelter last week and last month's four-week strike at Inco's Sudbury Ontario operations as factors affecting the market.
Both are key producers of plate nickel.
"Some producers are short and have had to cover," another trader said.
"There is also a perception that prices are low now which is helping business. I haven't noticed a summer lull."
Three months nickel was trading just above $6,800 per tonne on the London Metal Exchange (LME) on Tuesday, down some $400 from a month ago.
Meanwhile Western nickel plating was being quoted at a premium of around $300/$340 over LME cash in Rotterdam, compared to $290/$330 late last month, traders said.
A trader noted that business was also good in the United States and Asia. One-by-one (one inch square) cathodes were traded in the U.S. for a premium of $530 compared to $490 last week, he said.
Russian uncut nickel was also firmer, with the discount quoted around $70/$100, versus $80/$120 last month.
